raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Follow-up to #43164 (merged). The branch carries #43164's original commits and a merge of main, so against main the diff is only this change.

## Motivation

After #43164 (and #43327 / #43337), a profile of MiniMax-H3's pipelined Ulysses attention shows almost no exposed exchange left: 0.09–0.24 ms per layer. What remains on the SMs is the exchange's own data movement. Per head group and destination, two PyTorch strided copies run:

- v into the exchange block, from the fill;
- this rank's and each peer's rows into the merged output.

That is 28 elementwise copy kernels per layer at Ulysses 2 and 56 at Ulysses 4. Measured alone they move 0.8–1.4 TB/s (read plus write), and inside the pipeline they compete with FlashAttention, which wants every SM. Their SM time per layer, from isolated timings at the real shapes:

| Case (rows per rank) | merge copy | v copy | per layer | share of the layer |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Ref2VA, Ulysses 2 (24826) | 35.7 µs | 37.6 µs | 14 × 73 µs = 1.03 ms | 1.2% |
| T2VA, Ulysses 2 (18871) | 28.6 µs | 30.2 µs | 14 × 59 µs = 0.82 ms | 1.5% |
| T2VA, Ulysses 4 (9436) | 12.2 µs | 12.6 µs | 28 × 25 µs = 0.69 ms | 2.4% |

## Modifications

Every copy of the exchange now runs on the copy engine, as a pitched `cuMemcpy2DAsync` issued next to the stream memory operations it already uses. Nothing moves on the SMs, and the result stays bit-identical: it is pure data movement, and attention sees the same values.

- **Receive slots are split by part:** `[2, groups, 3, world, chunk]`. Group g's q, k and v from every rank are each one contiguous `[S, group_heads, head_dim]` tensor, and attention reads them directly.
- **v moves straight from the projection output** into every destination's receive slot, this rank's own included. It no longer passes through the send buffer.
- **q/k:**
  - With a `fill` (H3's QK-norm), the fill writes q and k into the send buffer, and one 2-row copy takes both to the peer.
  - Without a `fill`, q, k and v all move straight from their sources, and the pack kernel is gone.
- **The merge:** this rank's rows and each peer's rows land in their output block with a pitched copy on the group stream.
- **`fill(head_start, head_count, q_dst, k_dst)`** now writes only q and k.
- **Memory:** the send buffer holds q/k only, so the buffers are 10 × (rows per rank) × heads × head_dim instead of 11 ×, which is 3.6 GB for Ref2VA at Ulysses 2. The cookbook note says so.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test_ipc_a2a_multi_gpu.py` passes at 2 and 4 ranks. It compares against the sequential exchange byte for byte, with and without a fill, including the automatic group count and the head count that must decline.
- End to end on 4×H200, the MP4 md5 is unchanged in all twelve runs: T2VA at Ulysses 2 and 4, and Ref2VA at Ulysses 2.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Client end-to-end latency, 4×H200, 50 steps, default quality. These runs sit on top of #43164, #43327 and #43337. The arms ran ABBA on one box (without, with, with, without):

| Case | without | with | e2e | denoise stage |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| T2VA 5 s, 4 GPUs, Ulysses 4 | 71.66 / 71.69 s | 70.88 / 70.95 s | −1.06% | 69.88 → 69.09 s (−1.13%) |
| T2VA 5 s, 2 GPUs, Ulysses 2 | 140.40 / 140.38 s | 139.91 / 139.87 s | −0.36% | 136.63 → 135.82 s (−0.59%) |
| Ref2VA 5 s, 2 GPUs, Ulysses 2 | 218.50 / 218.74 s | 217.82 / 218.00 s | −0.32% | 212.27 → 211.07 s (−0.57%) |

The gain is largest at Ulysses 4, which ran 56 copy kernels per layer against 28 at Ulysses 2. It is below the SM time the copies held, because part of that time overlapped attention tails anyway, and the H200s sit at their 700 W cap, so part of the freed time comes back as a lower clock.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -1470,7 +1470,7 @@ fold decision is not node-boundary aware:
 - The released visual VAE quality recipe uses overlapping tiled decode. SGLang keeps that recipe by default and distributes complete tiles across the decode group; this changes scheduling, not the computation inside each tile.
 - H3 rejects `--vae-config.parallel-decode-mode spatial` and `spatial_shard`: validation found output mismatches. Use the default released tiled recipe.
 - Keep the default `--encoder-parallel auto`. With the server’s default `batching_max_size` of 1, single-node H100/H200/B200/B300 recipes with peer-to-peer access fold the Qwen text encoder over otherwise idle Ulysses ranks. This is separate from DiT tensor parallelism. A pure-TP recipe already shards the encoder over its TP group and does not add a world fold.
-- Single-node Ulysses recipes pipeline each block's all-to-all against dense FlashAttention over the copy engine: one head group's q/k/v moves while the previous group attends, and the output is bit-identical to the sequential exchange. It needs peer-to-peer access and stream memory operations on every rank and about 11 × (rows per rank) × heads × head_dim extra activations per rank (3.9 GB for Ref2VA at Ulysses 2); when that does not fit on some rank, every rank keeps the sequential exchange. `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_ULYSSES_PIPELINE_GROUPS=0` restores the sequential exchange.
+- Single-node Ulysses recipes pipeline each block's all-to-all against dense FlashAttention over the copy engine: one head group's q/k/v moves while the previous group attends, every copy (the merge into the output included) runs on the copy engine, and the output is bit-identical to the sequential exchange. It needs peer-to-peer access and stream memory operations on every rank and about 10 × (rows per rank) × heads × head_dim extra activations per rank (3.6 GB for Ref2VA at Ulysses 2); when that does not fit on some rank, every rank keeps the sequential exchange. `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_ULYSSES_PIPELINE_GROUPS=0` restores the sequential exchange.
 - For throughput-oriented serving, select **DP (batched throughput)**. The picker pairs `--encoder-parallel dp` with an editable `--batching-max-size` greater than 1. Encoder DP stays inside each DiT replica and composes with encoder TP: the H100 TP2 + Ulysses2 recipe has two TP-sharded encoder copies that can split a batch, while the RTX 5090 pure-TP2 recipe has one encoder copy and therefore no additional batch-DP degree. It provides no benefit for a batch of one and is not bitwise-identical to the unsplit deployment.
 - Use explicit **Fold** to prioritize single-request latency and encoder memory on a measured high-bandwidth single-node topology. Use **Replicate** as the compatibility path when folding or encoder DP is unsuitable.
 - `--use-fsdp-inference true` shards only the DiT. MiniMax-H3 preserves the original FP32 dtype of its patch, time, and output projections during FSDP all-gather, so this path does not trade numerical correctness for memory. On 4×H100, prefer TP2 + Ulysses2 for speed; use FSDP as an explicit capacity policy rather than assuming it is faster.
